questions.question: Oncoming vehicles are on your left. Parked vehicles are on your right. Where should you steer?

options.text: Closer to the oncoming vehicles.
Closer to the parked vehicles.
In the middle, between both sides.

questions.correctAnswerText: In the middle, between both sides.
questions.explanation: Steer down the middle of the road. This keeps you away from both the oncoming traffic and the parked cars.

questions.question: When passing another car, when should you move back to the right lane?

options.text: When you are one car length ahead of the other car.
When you can see both headlights of the other car in your rearview mirror.
When you are 50 feet ahead of the other car.

questions.correctAnswerText: When you can see both headlights of the other car in your rearview mirror.
questions.explanation: You need enough space between you and the car you passed before moving back. When you see both of that car's headlights in your mirror, it is safe to return to the right lane.

questions.question: What does this sign mean?

options.text: A railroad crossing is ahead. Be ready to stop.
You must always stop at the railroad crossing ahead.
Stop and wait for a signal before you cross the tracks.

questions.correctAnswerText: A railroad crossing is ahead. Be ready to stop.
questions.explanation: This sign tells you a railroad crossing is near. Look and listen carefully. Slow down and be ready to stop. Do not proceed until any trains have passed.

questions.question: A red light is showing, but a police officer tells you to go through the intersection. What should you do?

options.text: Stop and wait for the light to turn green.
Go through the intersection without stopping.
Come to a complete stop before proceeding.

questions.correctAnswerText: Go through the intersection without stopping.
questions.explanation: Police officers directing traffic have authority over traffic lights and signs. Always follow a police officer's directions.

questions.question: You are parking parallel on a hill facing downward. What should you do with your wheels?

options.text: Turn them sharply toward the curb or road edge.
Turn them away from the curb or road edge.
Keep them straight.

questions.correctAnswerText: Turn them sharply toward the curb or road edge.
questions.explanation: When parking downhill, turn your wheels toward the curb. This stops your car from rolling into traffic if the brakes fail.

questions.question: You are leaving an alley or driveway to enter the street. What must you do at the sidewalk?

options.text: Stop only if you see pedestrians.
Stop before driving onto the sidewalk.
Expect pedestrians to move out of your way.

questions.correctAnswerText: Stop before driving onto the sidewalk.
questions.explanation: You must stop before entering the sidewalk area. Pedestrians and traffic on the road have the right-of-way.

questions.question: When should you give up your legal right-of-way?

options.text: Often, even at controlled intersections.
Whenever it helps prevent a crash.
Never, because it confuses other drivers.

questions.correctAnswerText: Whenever it helps prevent a crash.
questions.explanation: Do not assume other drivers will give you the right-of-way. Give it up whenever you need to prevent a crash.

questions.question: You must give the right-of-way to pedestrians who are:

options.text: In a marked crosswalk.
In any crosswalk or intersection.
Crossing any street.

questions.correctAnswerText: Crossing any street.
questions.explanation: Always give the right-of-way to pedestrians crossing the street, whether the crosswalk is marked or not. For safety, yield to any person crossing any street.

questions.question: Your car is skidding and the rear end slides to the left. Which way should you steer?

options.text: To the right.
To the left.
Tap the brakes lightly and shift into neutral.

questions.correctAnswerText: To the left.
questions.explanation: In a skid, take your foot off the brake and steer in the direction you want the front of the car to go. If the rear slides left, steer left to straighten the vehicle.

questions.question: In bad weather, what should you do?

options.text: Steer off the road.
Drive in a low gear.
Steer and brake smoothly.

questions.correctAnswerText: Steer and brake smoothly.
questions.explanation: In bad weather, avoid hard braking and sharp turns. Smooth steering and braking help you keep control of your car.

questions.question: When entering the interstate, find a gap in traffic, match the speed of traffic, signal, and then:

options.text: Expect other drivers to let you in since you have the right-of-way.
Merge carefully into the gap.
Wait for the lane to completely clear before merging.

questions.correctAnswerText: Merge carefully into the gap.
questions.explanation: Find a gap in traffic, speed up to match other cars, and signal. Then merge into the gap when it is safe. Watch for other traffic and do not expect drivers to move out of your way.

questions.question: When driving at high speeds, signal ____ before you turn.

options.text: Two seconds
Four to five seconds
10 seconds

questions.correctAnswerText: Four to five seconds
questions.explanation: Use your turn signal before changing lanes or turning. At high speeds, signal four to five seconds before you move left or right.

questions.question: If cars keep passing you on both sides while you drive in the center lane of an expressway, you should:

options.text: Stay in the center lane.
Move to the right lane.
Move to the left lane.

questions.correctAnswerText: Move to the right lane.
questions.explanation: On roads with four or more lanes, drive in the right lanes unless you are passing or turning left. On an interstate, use the right lane if you are driving slower than other traffic.

questions.question: What does this sign mean?

options.text: Slow down when the pavement is wet.
The road ahead has curves.
Traffic will increase ahead.

questions.correctAnswerText: Slow down when the pavement is wet.
questions.explanation: Warning signs are yellow with black markings. This sign warns you that the road will be slippery when wet. Reduce your speed.

questions.question: What does this sign mean?

options.text: You can drive in either direction in this lane.
Traffic flows both ways on this road.
You are near a divided highway.

questions.correctAnswerText: Traffic flows both ways on this road.
questions.explanation: This sign warns you that traffic comes from both directions.

questions.question: When you prepare to turn left from a two-way street, drive:

options.text: On the right side of the road.
Near the center line.
On the left side of the center line.

questions.correctAnswerText: Near the center line.
questions.explanation: When turning left from a two-way street, stay in the lane closest to the center line. Begin your turn just before your car reaches the middle of the intersection. Do not cut the corner. Turn into the first available legal lane.

questions.question: If your car starts to skid, you should:

options.text: Pump the brakes.
Apply the brakes lightly.
Do not use the brakes.

questions.correctAnswerText: Do not use the brakes.
questions.explanation: Do not brake if your car skids. Keep steering until the car is under control and moving safely.

questions.question: If the road ahead is covered by heavy smoke, you should:

options.text: Turn on your flashers and keep driving.
Slow down, move to the right, and stop away from the road.
Turn on your high beams and keep driving.

questions.correctAnswerText: Slow down, move to the right, and stop away from the road.
questions.explanation: If you see heavy smoke ahead, slow down right away. Move as far right as you can and stop off the road. Then decide if it is safe to continue. Some smoke can harm your eyes and lungs.

questions.question: When you plan to pass another vehicle, you should:

options.text: Not assume the driver will make room for you to return to your lane.
Assume the driver will let you pass if you signal.
Assume the driver will keep the same speed.

questions.correctAnswerText: Not assume the driver will make room for you to return to your lane.
questions.explanation: Even if you signal, do not assume that other drivers will give you space or let you pass.

questions.question: Use your high beam headlights:

options.text: When there are no oncoming cars.
Where pedestrians may be present.
Both A and B.

questions.correctAnswerText: Both A and B.
questions.explanation: High beams let you see twice as far as low beams. Use them on unfamiliar roads, in work zones, or where people may be on the side of the road. Turn them off if other cars are nearby.

questions.question: If you cannot find a gap in traffic to enter the freeway, what should you do?

options.text: Keep your speed and force other drivers to make room.
Slow down on the ramp and wait for a gap.
Stop at the end of the ramp and wait for a gap.

questions.correctAnswerText: Slow down on the ramp and wait for a gap.
questions.explanation: Slow down on the ramp to wait for a gap in traffic. Do not stop at the end of the ramp because you will not have enough space to speed up to match traffic before entering the road.

questions.question: What does this sign mean?

options.text: Stop.
Merge.
Upcoming change in direction.

questions.correctAnswerText: Stop.
questions.explanation: A red, eight-sided sign means "stop."

questions.question: How can you avoid glare from an oncoming car's headlights?

options.text: Look briefly toward the right side of the road.
Focus on the centerline of the road.
Flash your high beams.

questions.correctAnswerText: Look briefly toward the right side of the road.
questions.explanation: Look briefly toward the right side of the road to avoid the bright lights from an oncoming vehicle. Then continue looking ahead to watch the other vehicle's position.

questions.question: If your vehicle has Anti-Lock Brakes (ABS), how should you stop on snow or ice?

options.text: Pump the brakes.
Press and hold the brake pedal firmly.
Release the brakes and let the car slow down on its own.

questions.correctAnswerText: Press and hold the brake pedal firmly.
questions.explanation: Press the brake pedal firmly and keep it pressed. The ABS will pump the brakes automatically, which is faster than you can pump them yourself.

questions.question: If you park facing uphill on a road with no curb, set the parking brake and:

options.text: Turn your wheels toward the edge of the road.
Turn your wheels away from the edge of the road.
Keep your wheels facing straight.

questions.correctAnswerText: Turn your wheels toward the edge of the road.
questions.explanation: Turn your wheels to the right, toward the edge of the road. If your brakes fail, the car will roll off the road instead of into traffic.
